instance: the nervous system as telegraph network

axes.material_environment: copper line, batteries, relay stations, coal-fired industry
axes.artifact: the electric telegraph — signal sent down a dedicated wire to a central office
axes.science_as_practised: a result was a traced line: stimulus in, signal along a nerve, response out, with a velocity attached
axes.epistemology: to know the system was to map its wiring and clock its signals

frame.claim: the nervous system is a telegraph network: messages travel along dedicated lines to a central office where they are read
frame.exterior: the operator who reads the message at the far end

criterion.name: understanding = trace the line from sender to receiver and time the signal

operands.name: discreteness of the message
operands.note: telegraph traffic is discrete because the key is; the nerve was granted the same

operands.name: the central office
operands.note: the network had an exchange, so a place where it all arrives was assumed

operands.name: dedicated line per message
operands.note: one wire, one circuit — a property of the installed plant

operands.name: who reads the message
operands.note: required by the frame at the receiving end and located nowhere in it
